fieldData.name: Topicweave
fieldData.summary: Topicweave turns a website that lists what you do into one that explains what you know: one shared vocabulary in your own words ties every service, project, article and answer together, so visitors, search engines and AI assistants can follow your expertise. An optional app and a Voice Kit keep it growing, and nothing publishes without you.
fieldData.objective-cadet: AI answers reward sites that connect the dots, and most expert sites don’t: services on one page, case studies on another, a blog nothing links to. Tracking tools can tell you you’re missing; they can’t build what’s missing. Topicweave installs the missing structure on the site you already have. Name your ideas in your own words, tag each page once, and topic pages, related reading and structured data build from those tags. An optional app reports on your topics, suggests what to write next and lets you capture ideas from your phone, with every draft waiting for your OK. Launch pricing isn’t set yet, so the site invites a few beta sites instead. This mission is that product site plus its prototypes, and a [[Test flight]].
fieldData.objective-engineer: Ten pages coded by hand after an ideation board and wireframes, sharing one look layer: data attributes on the root element pick the accent, typeface, corners and glass, so a design decision is one switch. The signature is a canvas loom: up to 1,700 threads on desktop and 620 on phones that weave the mark, then take a different shape for every section, paused offscreen and a still frame under [[Reduced motion]]. On phones, page changes knit a cloth from the link you tapped and unravel it on the next page. Four clickable prototypes (a dashboard with 17 views, a phone capture app, a CMS tagging panel and the monthly email) run on one set of sample data. No framework.
fieldData.params:
Name the ideas in the client’s words, not ours
Show it working, and label every sample as a sample
Nothing publishes without the owner’s OK
No promised rankings, citations or timelines
Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no framework

fieldData.name: The loom
fieldData.cadet: Colored threads weave the logo, then take a new shape for every section: scattered pieces, a ring of topics, a map, a finished cloth. It’s the idea of connecting what you know, drawn.
fieldData.why: A signature image people remember, and one that explains the product before a word is read.
fieldData.engineer: One canvas, drawn by hand. The thread count follows the screen (620 on phones, up to 1,700 on desktop), the pixel budget is capped on 4K screens, it pauses offscreen and in hidden tabs, and [[Reduced motion]] gets one still frame.

fieldData.name: One switch per decision
fieldData.cadet: Every page and every prototype shares one look: lilac accent, Fraunces headlines, square corners, glass panels.
fieldData.why: The look was chosen by trying options side by side, so each choice had to stay a single switch, not a hunt through stylesheets.
fieldData.engineer: The settled choices live as data attributes on the root element and one stylesheet keys off them, the same idea as [[Variables]] in Webflow. Changing the accent or the corners everywhere is one value.

fieldData.name: A cloth between pages
fieldData.cadet: On a phone, tapping a link knits a cloth of threads out from your finger, and the next page unravels it.
fieldData.why: Page changes are where a phone feels cheap. This one feels like the brand.
fieldData.engineer: The woven cloth repeats every four cells, so it’s one small tile drawn once and filled across every settled cell in a single call; only threads still in flight are drawn one by one. Bigger screens get a plain fade.

fieldData.name: Reports in your own topics
fieldData.cadet: The app groups search data by the vocabulary you signed off, so you see which ideas are growing and which have no proof yet.
fieldData.why: A wall of URLs tells an owner nothing. Their own topics do.
fieldData.engineer: Seventeen dashboard views on hash routes, one shared sample data file, light and dark. The health score shows its weights on screen, so it’s never a mystery.

fieldData.name: Nothing publishes without you
fieldData.cadet: Talk for a minute on your phone. It comes back as a draft in your words, tagged, and Publish stays locked until you approve it.
fieldData.why: The fear with AI writing is that it sounds generic and goes out on its own. The lock answers both.
fieldData.engineer: The phone prototype walks record, review and publish. Approving flips the button to Publish; there is no path that skips it.

fieldData.name: Tag once, connected everywhere
fieldData.cadet: Tag an entry with the ideas it proves and publish: the topic page, related reading and the structured data all update from that one field.
fieldData.why: “Tag once, linked everywhere” is abstract until you see one field turn into ten links.
fieldData.engineer: The links are written into the CMS as real references, not painted on by a script. [[JSON-LD]] is built from the same tags, so what search engines read always matches the page.

fieldData.name: Build what trackers only report
fieldData.problem: AI-visibility trackers tell expert businesses they’re missing from the answers, then leave them to fix it.
fieldData.fix: An install that builds the missing structure on the site they already have: a vocabulary, tagged pages, topic pages and structured data.
fieldData.result: The site gets clearer with every entry, instead of another report about why it isn’t.
fieldData.engineer: Tags are native CMS references, so the links survive without any script.

fieldData.name: Make the mechanism obvious
fieldData.problem: Vocabularies, tagging and structured data sound like a developer project.
fieldData.fix: The loom draws the idea section by section, from scattered pieces to a finished cloth, and the tag-once demo shows one field becoming ten links.
fieldData.result: The idea lands in seconds, with no jargon on screen.
fieldData.engineer: Every section names the shape it wants; the loom reads it and re-forms as you scroll.

fieldData.name: Keep it in their voice
fieldData.problem: Owners expect AI drafts to sound generic, and worry something will publish without them.
fieldData.fix: A Voice Kit filled in about 15 minutes from their own writing and a short recording, and a review queue where Publish stays locked until they approve.
fieldData.result: Drafts start from their own sentences, and they stay the author.
fieldData.engineer: Every piece moves Draft → In review → Approved; zero auto-publishing is the rule, not a setting.

fieldData.name: Earn trust by not overselling
fieldData.problem: Most “get found by AI” pitches promise rankings and citations nobody can guarantee.
fieldData.fix: “AI visibility, honestly”: two signals shown as signals, sample data labeled in every prototype, and no promised outcomes.
fieldData.result: The site reads like the expert, not the salesperson.
fieldData.engineer: No logos, testimonials, customer counts or rankings anywhere; every simulated screen says so.

fieldData.name: A beta instead of a guess
fieldData.problem: Launch pricing isn’t set, and a price list would have been a guess.
fieldData.fix: A beta: a few sites get the install now, by hand, far below the launch price, for honest feedback. Every call to action says Join the beta, and a public roadmap shows what’s coming.
fieldData.result: Early sites get a fair deal, and the product meets real sites before it launches.
fieldData.engineer: Pricing shows the packages with TBD and a time calculator, so the value is clear before the price is.
